title: One Sleep Rule Cut The SIDS Rate In Half
hook: Putting babies on their backs turned a deadly bedtime risk around.
closing: Back sleeping cut the risk dramatically, but consistent safe sleep still matters.
question: Do new parents know this rule?

segments.say: The SIDS rate fell to 0.64 per thousand births, less than half its earlier level. One sleep change worked.
Before the campaign, 85.4 percent of SIDS cases involved stomach-down placement. Back sleeping targeted the dominant risk.
About 3,400 sleep-related infant deaths still occur yearly. The rule reduced danger without eliminating it.
